chapters.title: Updates around the room
chapters.gist: Daniel is 23 of 31 on the GA checklist but has a solver regression on 500+ stop routes; Kenji found urban-dense ETA error at 7.6 min and is prototyping a dock-wait feature; Ravi's retry-with-jitter PR is in review and his circuit breaker spike is half done; Priya is exploring a tracking page just in case.

chapters.title: Blocker: staging Redis for failover testing
chapters.gist: Daniel can't run the GA failover test because Ravi's prod-like staging Redis cluster is tied up by the circuit breaker spike; they agree to time-share it for a week (Ravi mornings, Daniel afternoons from Monday) and Daniel will write down the pass bar.

chapters.title: Wrap-up and Q4 planning prep
chapters.gist: Maya reminds everyone that Q4 planning is at 4pm and asks each person to bring engineer-week estimates; live ETA versus onboarding is expected to be the main debate.

turns.t: Okay, morning, afternoon, whatever it is for everyone. Let's do it quick, I know Friday's packed and we've got planning later. Daniel, you want to kick us off?

Yeah, sure. So, GA checklist. I went through it again yesterday with, uh, with the stuff we added after the beta review, and we're at, I think twenty-three of thirty-one items closed. Most of what's left is boring, it's like runbooks, the alerting dashboards, the rollback doc. The one that's not boring is the solver regression. So on routes with more than five hundred stops, solve time went from, it was around nine seconds on the old build and now the p95 is like forty-one seconds. Forty-ish. And it's only the big routes, under five hundred it's fine, it's basically flat. I'm pretty sure it's the time-window constraint change we merged last week, because if I flip that flag off it goes right back to normal. So today I'm bisecting that properly and, yeah, I want to see if it's the constraint itself or just how we're seeding the initial solution, because my gut says it's the seeding.
Which fleets actually have five-hundred-plus stop routes in the beta?

Honestly, only one regularly. The parcel fleet, the, uh, the one in Columbus. But freight-wise Harbor & Pine would have a bunch of those if they sign, they do these long consolidated runs, so I don't want to just shrug at it.
No, agreed. Is it a GA blocker in your head?
Right now, yes. If I can get it under fifteen seconds I'd downgrade it to a known issue. I'll know more Monday.
Okay. Do you need anything from anyone for the bisect?

No, it's just me and a lot of coffee. Well, actually, Kenji, did anything change on your side last week? Because the seeding pulls from the ETA matrix, so if the calls got slower that would show up exactly there.
Not the model. I bumped the feature service client version on, I think Tuesday, but that shouldn't change latency. I can check the traces though.
Yeah, if you could just look, so I can rule it out.
Okay. Kenji, you're up anyway.

Yeah. So the ETA model, overall we're still at four point three minutes mean absolute error, that hasn't moved. But I split it out by stop density this week, and for the urban-dense bucket, so like more than, I think I used forty stops per square kilometer, it's way worse, it's around seven point eight. Sorry, seven point six, I re-ran it last night. Seven point six. And a lot of that is dock wait. Like the van arrives on time, technically, and then sits at a loading dock for twelve minutes and the model has no idea that's going to happen. So the dock-wait feature, I've got a first version that uses historical dwell time per address, per hour of day, and on the offline eval it takes the dense bucket down to about six. Which is better. Not great, but better.
Is that per address or per geofence? Because a lot of those docks have like three addresses.
Per address right now. Yeah, I know. I want to cluster them, that's the next thing.
Where's the dense bucket mostly coming from? Like which fleets?

Brightside, mostly. Their downtown routes in the apartment-heavy areas, and grocery is this weird mix of residential drop-offs and store docks. Which is also, yeah, the fleet that's least happy with us right now, so.
Right. Okay, that's useful for planning. And timeline-wise, is dock wait making it into GA or is that a fast-follow?

I think fast-follow. I don't really want to ship a feature change to the model like six weeks before GA without a full beta cycle on it. But I'll have the clustered numbers by Wednesday so we can decide properly instead of me just guessing.
That works. Ravi.
Yeah, hi. So the retry-with-jitter PR is up, it's in review, Daniel's got it, no pressure.
I'm on it, I'm on it. This afternoon.

Cool. So that's the direct fix for the retry storm from last Thursday. The dispatch workers were all retrying on a fixed interval when Redis failed over, so they basically hammered the ETA service in lockstep and it just fell over. I pulled the numbers for the postmortem, during those forty-seven minutes the request rate on the ETA service was like thirty x normal. Thirty-two x. So now it's exponential backoff with full jitter and a cap on attempts. And then separately I'm doing a spike on a circuit breaker in front of the ETA service, so if it starts failing, the workers stop calling it and fall back to the last known ETA instead of piling on. The spike's maybe half done. I've got it running in staging and I'm basically killing the primary over and over and watching what the workers do.
Nice. And the postmortem doc, that's done?
Draft is done. I want Sofia to read the customer-impact section before it goes wide, because she's the one who's been fielding Brightside all week, so, Monday.
Great. Priya, anything from you? I know you're mostly heads-down on onboarding.

Yeah, mostly onboarding. The one thing for this group is I've been doing some tracking-page explorations, like the customer-facing live ETA page. Just in case. It's not committed, I know. I just don't want us starting from a blank page if it does get prioritized at planning.
Totally fair. Just keep it clearly labeled as exploration so nobody sees it in Figma and thinks it's happening.
It literally says exploration in the file name.
If it does happen, it'd be using the same ETA, right? So the dense urban error would show up right in front of the end customer.
Yeah, that's partly why I'm poking at it. Like how we show uncertainty instead of a fake precise time.
Good point. Let's park that for planning.
Okay, Daniel, you flagged a blocker in Slack.

Yeah. So part of the GA checklist is a failover test. We said after last week we're not shipping v3 without proving the new routing path survives a Redis failover. And the only staging Redis cluster that's actually set up like prod, with the replicas and the sentinel config, is Ravi's. Which he's using for the circuit breaker spike. So I've basically been waiting on it since Tuesday.
Yeah, that's on me. I sort of took it over.
No, it's the right use of it. It's just that we both need to kill the primary and we can't both do that at the same time, it'd just be noise in both our results.
Can we spin up a second one?

We can, it's not hard, it's Terraform, but the prod-like config is like eight nodes and the staging budget is, I'd need to ask. And honestly it's a day of me fiddling with it to get the sentinel stuff matching. I'd rather time-share. For my spike I can do my runs in the morning. Like I'm done by noon Pacific most days, and Daniel can have it after that.
How much is the budget thing, ballpark?
Eight nodes for a month, it's not crazy, a couple thousand bucks maybe. It's more my time than the money.
Okay. Let's try time-share for a week, and if it's painful I'll go ask for the budget. I'd rather spend the money than have Daniel blocked on a GA item.
Time-share works for me. Actually it's better, because I want to run the failover test with your jitter change in, so if it's merged by Monday I'm testing the real thing and not the old retry logic.
Right, yeah. So review my PR today and you get the cluster Monday afternoon.
Ha. Deal.

I love a hostage negotiation. Okay, so, just to say it back. Ravi has the staging cluster mornings, Daniel has it afternoons starting Monday, Daniel reviews the jitter PR today so it can be merged and included in the failover test. Ravi, can you put that in the staging channel so nobody else wanders in and runs a load test on it?
Yep, I'll post it and pin it.
One more thing on that. When I do the failover I want to see the ETA service dashboards, the ones you set up after the outage. Am I gonna have access?
You should, they're in the platform folder in Grafana. If not, ping me and I'll add you.
And Daniel, what does done look like for the failover test? Like what's the pass bar?

I was thinking, we kill the primary under normal beta load, the routing path recovers inside sixty seconds, no retry spike over, say, two x baseline on the ETA service, and no ETAs older than five minutes served to the dispatcher dashboard. Something like that. I'll write it down properly.
Write it down and put it in the checklist doc. That's basically the thing I want to show Asher at the go, no-go.
Can I get a heads-up when you run it? I want to see what the model does when it gets stale features for a minute.
Sure, I'll ping the channel before each run.
Okay. Anything else? Priya, you're good?
All good.

Okay, last thing. Q4 planning is at four today, Asher's running it. Please come with your rough Q4 asks, like real numbers, engineer-weeks, not vibes. Daniel, I'd love a line on whether the solver thing changes the GA date, even if the answer is we don't know yet. Kenji, the dock-wait fast-follow. Ravi, the reliability stuff, the circuit breaker plus whatever else came out of the postmortem. And Priya, you'll have onboarding, obviously.
Is live ETA going to come up?
Oh, it's going to come up. It competes with onboarding for the same people, so, yeah, expect a debate.
Great. Love that for me.
Should I bring the failover pass bar to planning too, or is that too in the weeds for that room?
Too in the weeds. Just say the failover test is scheduled for next week. Asher cares that it's happening, not the thresholds.
Oh, and reminder, I'm out Thursday afternoon, dentist. So if the cluster catches fire Thursday, Daniel, it's all yours.
Great. Thanks, man.
That's it. Thanks everyone, see you at four.
Thanks.
Later.

general.tldr: Routing v3 GA checklist is 23/31 but a solver regression (p95 9s → 41s on 500+ stop routes) is a GA blocker for now, and the failover test was unblocked by time-sharing Ravi's staging Redis cluster from Monday.

items.text: Friday stand-up for the Routing squad ahead of the 4pm Q4 planning meeting.
GA checklist is at 23 of 31; the remaining non-trivial item is a solver regression on 500+ stop routes (p95 ~9s → ~41s), likely from last week's time-window constraint change.
Daniel treats the regression as a GA blocker unless he gets it under 15 seconds; he'll know more Monday.
Urban-dense ETA error is 7.6 min vs. 4.3 min overall; a first dock-wait feature brings it to ~6 min offline but is likely a post-GA fast-follow.
Staging Redis conflict resolved: Ravi gets the prod-like cluster mornings, Daniel afternoons from Monday, for a one-week trial before Maya asks for budget for a second cluster.
Only one beta fleet (the Columbus parcel fleet) regularly runs 500+ stop routes, but Harbor & Pine's consolidated freight runs would hit it if they sign.
Daniel suspects the solution seeding rather than the constraint itself; the seeding reads the ETA matrix, so Kenji will check whether his feature-service client bump added latency.

sections.heading: ETA accuracy in dense urban areas

items.text: Dock-wait feature uses historical dwell time per address and hour of day; Daniel pointed out docks often span several addresses, so Kenji will cluster them next.
Most of the dense-bucket error comes from Brightside's downtown grocery routes, the least happy fleet right now.
Retry-with-jitter PR (exponential backoff, full jitter, capped attempts) directly fixes the Sep 24 retry storm, when ETA service traffic hit ~32x normal.
Circuit breaker spike is about half done: workers would fall back to the last known ETA instead of piling on.
Postmortem draft is done; Sofia reviews the customer-impact section before it goes wide on Monday.
Proposed pass bar: recover within 60s under beta load, ETA retries under 2x baseline, and no ETAs older than 5 minutes on the dispatcher dashboard.
Maya wants the pass bar in the checklist doc as evidence for Asher's go/no-go.
Daniel reviews the jitter PR this afternoon so it's merged before his failover test.
Everyone brings engineer-week estimates to Q4 planning at 4pm; expect a live ETA vs. onboarding debate.

highlights.title: Solver regression on 500+ stop routes could block GA
Dense urban ETA error is 7.6 min, mostly dock wait

ask.q: Is the solver regression going to block Routing v3 GA?
ask.a: Possibly. On routes with 500+ stops, p95 solve time went from about 9s to about 41s, apparently from last week's time-window constraint change. Daniel considers it a GA blocker unless he can get it under 15 seconds, and expects to know more Monday after bisecting.

ask.q: What was blocking the failover test and how was it resolved?
ask.a: The only prod-like staging Redis cluster was in use by Ravi's circuit breaker spike, and both needed to kill the primary. They agreed to time-share for a week: Ravi uses it mornings, Daniel afternoons from Monday. If that's painful, Maya will ask for budget for a second cluster.

ask.q: How accurate is the ETA model on dense urban routes?
ask.a: Much worse than average: 7.6 minutes MAE in the urban-dense bucket vs. 4.3 overall, mostly from loading-dock wait. Kenji's first dock-wait feature gets it to about 6 minutes offline, but he leans toward shipping it as a post-GA fast-follow.

ask.q: What is being done to prevent another retry storm?
ask.a: Ravi's PR replaces fixed-interval retries with exponential backoff, full jitter and a cap on attempts. He is also spiking a circuit breaker so workers fall back to the last known ETA instead of hammering a failing ETA service. During the Sep 24 outage, ETA traffic hit about 32x normal.

ask.q: Is the team building the live ETA tracking page?
ask.a: Not yet. Priya is doing explorations only, clearly labeled as such, so the team isn't starting from a blank page if it gets prioritized. Maya expects it to be debated against onboarding at the 4pm Q4 planning meeting.
